title: Vanilla Cupcakes with Vanilla Buttercream
summary: Light, tender vanilla cupcakes topped with tall swirls of vanilla buttercream, baked in paper cases for an easy, shareable sweet.
equipment: 12-hole muffin tin lined with paper cases
stand mixer or electric hand whisk
piping bag with a large star nozzle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt
cake flour (or plain flour; see note)
ingredients.note: plain flour works with a slightly firmer crumb

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) with a shelf in the middle, allowing at least 20 minutes for it to come fully up to temperature. A properly heated oven helps the small amount of batter in each case rise quickly and evenly.

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Cream the butter, caster sugar and salt together for 3-4 minutes, beating until pale and fluffy, to build the light, vanilla-scented base of the batter. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well between each, then mix in the vanilla extract. This creaming stage traps the air that gives the cupcakes their light texture.

steps.title: Fold in flour and milk
steps.text: On low speed, add the flour and baking powder in two additions, alternating with the milk, mixing just until the batter is smooth. Stopping as soon as the flour disappears keeps the crumb tender rather than tight.

steps.title: Fill the cases
steps.text: Divide the batter between the paper cases, filling each about two-thirds full; an ice-cream scoop helps keep the amounts even. Leaving headroom gives the batter space to rise without spilling over the sides.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.text: Bake for 18-22 minutes, until the tops are golden, spring back when touched, and a skewer comes out clean. By this stage the batter's structure has fully set, so the cupcakes hold their shape as they cool.

steps.title: Cool before icing
steps.text: Leave the cupcakes in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely. Piping buttercream onto a warm cupcake melts it, so patience here keeps the swirl neat.

steps.title: Make the buttercream
steps.text: Beat the butter on its own for 3 minutes until very pale, then add the icing sugar on low speed. Mix in the milk, vanilla and salt, then beat on medium-high for 3-4 minutes until light and fluffy. The long beating time is what makes the buttercream airy rather than dense.

steps.title: Pipe and finish
steps.text: Once the cupcakes are completely cold, pipe tall swirls of buttercream on top using a star nozzle. Serve as soon as you like, or chill briefly first if the kitchen is warm.

tips: Fill the cases two-thirds full, not more – overfilled cases spill over the sides and bake unevenly.
Beat the butter and sugar for the full time stated; rushing this step traps less air and leaves denser cupcakes.
Let the cupcakes cool completely before piping, or the buttercream will melt and slide off.
Mix in the milk gently at the end rather than overmixing, since too much beating once it's added can toughen the crumb.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep iced cupcakes in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or in the fridge for up to 4 days. Unfrosted sponge freezes for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature before icing.
